post_text: Uku Joost Annus Raises €615K to Scale AI-Powered Mobile App Building. Estonian startup bilt.me has raised €614,900 ($700,000) in pre-seed funding to expand its AI-native platform that lets users turn an idea into a working mobile application. The round was led by Superhero Capital, with participation from Bolt founder Markus Villig and Lightyear founder Martin Sokk. Founded in August 2025, bilt.me began as a hackathon project in Tallinn before evolving into a platform focused specifically on native mobile applications. Its early traction is notable: thousands of people are already building on the platform, while revenue has surpassed six figures in annual recurring revenue.

post_text: “How do you get ideas for posts?” People ask me this a lot, here's how: 1. I have a doc where I store ideas throughout the day/week, not full drafts, just a quick note on the idea. 2. I take lots of pictures, especially for LinkedIn this is helpful since they seem to boost posts with photos. 3. pull from different buckets. Personal life, work life, humor, learnings, experiences/stories, hot takes/beliefs. 4. start small. 5. be consistent, pick a number and commit to it. 6. follow cool people. At the end of the day, there's pretty much zero downside and unlimited upside to posting on here.

post_text: Here's why honesty will take you far in the age of AI, fast outcomes, and big promises. I had a call today with a SaaS founder who wanted to start running ads (they are just starting out, no PMF). I asked him, 'Okay, can you tell me why people should choose your platform and who your ICP is?' Guess what... silence. Then I shared my approach to his product. He told me once again, 'But we have the budget.' I said, 'anybody who would take your money to start running ads for you right now would be a thief.' He appreciated it. We didn't move forward. I could have easily closed this deal, but that's just not how I see our team.

Two years ago, we set out with a crazy ambitious goal: rebuild the entire GTM stack from scratch. We'd tried everything out there, but nothing felt like the future. Today, Zero is used by hundreds of AI-native startups to run their GTM end-to-end. And I'm excited to share that we've raised a $10.3M seed round. AI has made it so much easier to build a product. It hasn't made it easier to build a business around one. Marketing, sales, and customer success teams still spend too much time switching between tools and keeping data up to date. We've been building quietly for two years.
